---

---
title: CLI Commands
description: Complete reference for the kod binary — every subcommand, its flags, and its purpose.
sidebar:
  order: 1
type: reference
---

import { Aside, Code } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod [--verbose] [<COMMAND>]`} />

KOD's CLI is a single binary with subcommands grouped by purpose: sessions, models, inspection, and audit. Most commands operate on the effective configuration (defaults merged with `~/.config/kod/config.toml` and any project policy) and talk to the model server configured under `[llm]`. Bare `kod` — no subcommand — prints an onboarding summary: entry points, config path, and discovered skill directories.

Global flag: `--verbose` turns up logging across the run — most useful with `agent` and `swarm` when you want to see the loop breathe.

Policy flag: where shown, `--preset` accepts `read-only` (alias `readonly`), `standard` (alias `default`), or `yolo` (alias `unrestricted`) and overrides the global config and any project `.kod/policy.toml` for that run.

## Commands at a glance

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `chat` | Start a chat session (plain REPL) with streaming output |
| `tui` | Launch the interactive terminal UI |
| `agent` | Run a single agent against a goal, then exit |
| `prompt` | Run one prompt non-interactively and print the reply |
| `run` | Run one prompt and stream the reply to stdout |
| `swarm` | Decompose a goal, run N agents concurrently, merge results |
| `serve` | Start (or stop) the long-lived engine daemon |
| `skills` | Work with skills: list, scaffold, edit, search, rename, copy, export |
| `validate-skills` | Validate every skill file; exits non-zero on malformed ones |
| `config` | Show, validate, export, edit, or seed the configuration |
| `models` | List models the configured provider offers |
| `profile` | List, show, or switch model profiles |
| `theme` | List or print the TUI themes |
| `sessions` | Show, export, import, or clear the saved TUI session |
| `memory` | Inspect, export, import, or clear long-term memory |
| `map` | Print the repository map used for prompt grounding |
| `replay` | Re-run the tool calls from a session log |
| `checkpoint` | List, diff, restore, or clear file-level undo snapshots |
| `policy` | Show the effective policy, or explain one hypothetical call |
| `tools` | List the tool registry, or show one tool's schema |
| `sandbox` | Check that the platform sandbox primitive is available |
| `doctor` | Print a diagnostics report; exits non-zero on failure |
| `init` | First-run helper; writes a default config if none exists |
| `test` | Run the built-in self-tests |
| `completions` | Print a shell completion script |
| `update` | Check GitHub for a newer release (read-only) |
| `validate-skills-strict` | Like `validate-skills`, but a skill missing a `version` also fails |
| `acp` | Run the Agent Client Protocol bridge on stdin/stdout (spawned by an editor) |
| `commit-check` | Validate a proposed conventional-commit message against the staged changes |
| `if-bench` | Run the working-memory + instruction-following eval against the default endpoint |
| `fixture` | Capture or replay a deterministic streaming fixture |
| `jev` | Jev (TypeSafe AI) status, statistics, and threshold tuning |
| `budget` | Session cost and limits |
| `limits` | Per-tool quotas and counters |
| `plan` | Print the plan artifact for the current session |
| `decisions` | Print the durable decisions recorded for the current session |
| `trace` | Inspect the structured turn traces in `turns.jsonl` |
| `__sandbox-exec` | Hidden: apply a Landlock sandbox to the current process and exec a command |

## `kod chat`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod chat [--model <name>] [--temperature <f>] [-i, --interactive]
         [--system-prompt <text>] [--sandbox] [--preset <preset>]`} />

Starts a plain REPL with streaming output. `--model` overrides the configured model for this session. `--temperature` (default `0.7`) is accepted for compatibility; the temperature actually applied comes from the endpoint config. `--system-prompt` replaces the built-in system prompt. `--sandbox` routes shell commands through `bwrap`/`sandbox-exec` and fails loudly when the primitive is unavailable. `--preset` overrides the policy for this session.

## `kod tui`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod tui [--model <name>] [--sandbox] [--preset <preset>] [--no-resume]`} />

Launches the interactive terminal UI. `--no-resume` is intended to skip the saved session; today it prints a hint instead — to start fresh, move `~/.kod/tui_session.json` aside.

## `kod agent`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod agent [-n <name>] -g "<goal>" [--model <name>] [--preset <preset>]`} />

One-shot agent run: classify the task, ground the prompt, call tools, finish with a summary. `-n, --name` (default `kod-agent`) labels the agent in logs; `-g, --goal` is required. Writes that need approval are refused (nothing interactive to approve) — see [Policy](/guides/policy/).

## `kod prompt`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod prompt <prompt> [--model <name>] [--no-log] [--sandbox]
           [--remote] [--socket <path>]`} />

One prompt, one reply, exit code 0 on success and 1 on error. Only the reply is printed to stdout; diagnostics go to stderr, so it pipes cleanly. `-` reads the prompt text from stdin. `--no-log` skips the session log entry. `--remote` sends the prompt to a running `kod serve` daemon instead of building an in-process engine (`--socket` overrides the socket path).

## `kod run`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod run <prompt> [--model <name>]`} />

Like `prompt`, but streams the reply to stdout as it is generated. `-` reads the prompt from stdin.

## `kod swarm`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod swarm -g "<goal>" [-n <agents>] [--model <name>] [--merge]`} />

Runs the full swarm pipeline. `-n, --agents` defaults to `swarm.max_agents` from config and is clamped to 2–8 by the runner. Merging is controlled by `swarm.merge_results` in the config; there is no `--no-merge` flag.

## `kod serve`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod serve [--stop] [--socket <path>]`} />

Starts a long-lived engine behind a Unix socket (default `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/kod.sock`, or `~/.kod/run/kod.sock` on macOS; never TCP) that `kod prompt --remote` attaches to. `--stop` asks a running daemon to exit and waits for the socket file to disappear.

## `kod skills`

`kod skills` with no subcommand lists the merged skills from every standard directory; `--json` emits the machine-readable inventory. Subcommands:

| Subcommand | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `list` | Same as bare `kod skills` |
| `new <name>` | Scaffold a new skill in the first writable directory; refuses to overwrite |
| `remove <name>` | Delete a skill; refuses without `--yes` unless inside the current directory |
| `edit <name>` | Open the file in `$EDITOR` |
| `show <name>` | Print the full markdown (front matter + body) |
| `search <query>` | Search by name, description, tags, or capabilities |
| `source <name>` | Print the absolute file path — useful for scripts |
| `rename <from> <to>` | Rename; rewrites the `name:` field; refuses if the destination exists |
| `copy <from> <to>` | Copy within the same directory; rewrites `name:`; refuses to overwrite |
| `export <name> <dest>` | Copy to a path or `-` for stdout; `--force` overwrites |

Two standalone validators complement the tree: `kod validate-skills` (exits non-zero on malformed skill files) and `kod validate-skills-strict` (additionally fails skills missing a `version`).

## `kod config`

| Subcommand | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| *(none)* | Print the effective config |
| `export [path]` | Write the effective config (defaults + user) to a file or `-`; `--force` overwrites |
| `path` | Print the config file location |
| `edit` | Open the config in `$EDITOR` (or `$VISUAL`, or `vi`) |
| `validate` | Parse and validate; exits non-zero on error — CI-friendly |
| `show-merged` | Print the effective config as TOML (reproducible) |
| `show-raw` | Print the raw file contents verbatim, comments included |
| `init-from <profile>` | Back up current config (`config.toml.bak-<unix-ts>`) and write one seeded from a profile |

## `kod profile`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod profile list [--json]              # show the built-in presets
kod profile show                       # print the effective [llm] config
kod profile use <profile> [--dry-run]  # write preset values into config.toml`} />

Presets: `local-fast`, `local-capable`, `local-reasoning`, `cloud-openai`. See [Model Profiles](/guides/profiles/).

## `kod models`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod models [--filter <text>]`} />

Lists models the configured provider offers (`--filter` is a case-insensitive substring match). Errors from the provider are surfaced rather than collapsed into an empty list, so a bad endpoint is visible here.

## `kod theme`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod theme list          # built-in theme names
kod theme show <name>   # one theme's palette as JSON (dark | light)`} />

## `kod sessions`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod sessions show                        # where the TUI session lives, message count
kod sessions export [path] [--format markdown|json]   # default stdout, Markdown
kod sessions import <path>               # replace saved session from JSON
kod sessions latest                      # path of the newest session log
kod sessions count                       # number of logs and combined size
kod sessions clear                       # delete the saved session file`} />

`export`/`import` round-trip: only `--format json` output can be imported back.

## `kod memory`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod memory list                  # every long-term entry, newest first
kod memory search <query>        # case-insensitive substring search
kod memory delete <short-id>     # remove one entry (id from list/search)
kod memory export [path]         # dump entries to a JSON file or \`-\`
kod memory import [path]         # append entries from a JSON file or \`-\`
kod memory clear [--yes]         # delete every entry; prompts without --yes`} />

## `kod map`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod map [--max-chars <n>]`} />

Prints the repository map (top-level symbols per recognised source file) used for prompt grounding. The cap defaults to 16000 characters (~4k tokens).

## `kod replay`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod replay <session.jsonl> [--execute]`} />

Re-runs the tool calls recorded in a session log, without the model. Without `--execute` it prints what would run; with `--execute` it performs the calls for real.

## `kod checkpoint`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod checkpoint list [--limit <n>]   # snapshots for this project (default 20)
kod checkpoint diff <id>            # unified diff: snapshot vs current file
kod checkpoint restore <id>         # restore the file; the snapshot is kept
kod checkpoint clear                # delete every checkpoint for this directory`} />

## `kod policy`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod policy show
kod policy explain <tool> [key=value …]`} />

`show` prints the effective policy with each rule's provenance. `explain` answers “what would the engine decide for this call?” without running anything — for example `kod policy explain write_file path=src/main.rs`. Values that parse as JSON are used as JSON; anything else is treated as a string. CLI `--preset` overrides are deliberately not applied.

## `kod tools`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod tools list        # every registered tool
kod tools show <name> # one tool's name, description, schema, permissions`} />

## `kod sandbox`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod sandbox check`} />

Reports whether the platform sandbox primitive is available — and the install command when it is not.

## `kod doctor`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod doctor [--json] [--fix]`} />

Diagnostics for config, endpoint, skills, memory, sandbox, and git. Exits non-zero if any check fails, so it can gate a script or CI. `--fix` creates missing directories and writes a default config if none exists; it never modifies an existing config file.

## `kod init`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod init [--force]`} />

Ensures a config file exists (backing up the old one with `--force`), prints where it lives, and prints the next three commands a new user should run. Idempotent.

## `kod completions` / `kod test` / `kod update`

<Code lang="bash" code={`kod completions <bash|zsh|fish|elvish|powershell>   # completion script on stdout
kod test                                            # built-in self-tests
kod update                                          # check GitHub for a newer release`} />

<Aside type="tip">
  Scripting against KOD? <code>kod prompt</code> (clean stdout, exit codes) and <code>kod doctor --json</code> / <code>kod skills --json</code> (machine-readable) are the stable surfaces to build on.
</Aside>


---

---
title: Config Reference
description: Every configuration key KOD reads — section, type, default, and notes — in one table.
sidebar:
  order: 4
type: reference
---

import { Aside, Code } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The config file lives at `~/.config/kod/config.toml` (Linux) or `~/Library/Application Support/kod/config.toml` (macOS), is auto-generated on first run, and every key below is optional — out-of-range values are clamped into valid ranges at load time with a warning. A missing or corrupt file falls back to defaults rather than failing the session.

## `[llm]`

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `network_access` | bool | `false` | Opt-in network access; gates `web_fetch`. Per-tool `network` in `.kod/policy.toml` overrides. |

## `[[llm.endpoints]]`

An array of named model servers; the first is the default. Everything that affects the wire lives on the endpoint.

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | `"default"` | Routing key referenced by `[llm.routing]`; duplicate names warn. |
| `provider` | string | `"openai-compatible"` | `"Ollama"` and `"OpenAI"` are aliases of `openai-compatible`. `"anthropic"` is recognised but fails at the first prompt. |
| `base_url` | URL | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | Normalised automatically — server root or `.../v1` root both work. |
| `model` | string | `"codellama:13b"` | Must exist on the server; what `kod models` lists. |
| `api_key_env` | string (optional) | — | Name of the env var holding the API key. The key itself never appears in the file. |
| `temperature` | float (optional) | `0.7` | Clamped to 0.0–2.0 at load. |
| `max_tokens` | integer (optional) | `2048` | Generation cap; `0` falls back to the default. |
| `context_window` | integer | `8192` | Sizes the memory budget and the context meter; clamped to ≥ 2000. |
| `timeout_secs` | integer | `300` | Per-request timeout; floored at 1. |
| `pricing.input_per_mtok_usd` | float (optional) | — | USD per million input tokens, for the TUI cost display. |
| `pricing.output_per_mtok_usd` | float (optional) | — | USD per million output tokens. |

## `[llm.routing]`

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `by_task` | map: task type → endpoint name | — | `"Simple"`, `"Debugging"`, … route to the named endpoint. Unknown names are dropped with a warning. |
| `fallback` | list of endpoint names | — | Ordered retry chain when the primary fails with a retryable error. |
| `swarm` | map: capability → endpoint name | — | `Planning`, `Coding`, … route swarm roles to different models. |

## `[memory]`

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `short_term_capacity` | integer | `100` | FIFO entries kept for the session. |
| `scope` | `"global"` \| `"project"` | `"global"` | `project` puts the long-term DB at `<cwd>/.kod/memory.redb`; `global` uses `~/.kod/data/kod.redb`. |
| `long_term_db_path` | string (optional) | — | Overrides both scopes with an explicit `redb` path. |
| `enable_semantic_search` | bool | `true` | Applies when an embedding endpoint is configured; retrieval is keyword + recency otherwise. |
| `embedding_endpoint` | `"none"` \| `"ollama"` \| `"openai"` | `"none"` | `ollama` derives the URL from `llm.base_url`; `openai` speaks `/v1/embeddings`. |
| `embedding_url` | string (optional) | — | Explicit embedder URL, overriding the derived one. |
| `embedding_api_key_env` | string (optional) | — | Env var holding the embedder API key (openai endpoint). |
| `embedding_model` | string | `"nomic-embed-text"` | Model name sent to the embedder. |
| `context_window` | integer | `4096` | Memory manager fallback budget. |
| `compaction_interval_secs` | integer | `3600` | Long-term store compaction cadence. |
| `extract_on_shutdown` | bool | `false` | One LLM call at session end pulls durable facts from the transcript. |
| `extract_max_entries` | integer | `12` | Cap on facts extracted per session. |

## `[skills]`

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enable_hot_reload` | bool | `true` | Edits to skill files apply on the next prompt. |
| `max_skills_per_query` | integer | `3` | Skills matched per prompt, capped. |
| `skills_dir` | string (optional) | — | Replaces the four standard search directories with one custom path. |
| `match_threshold` | float | `0.3` | Minimum match score for a skill to ride along. Calibrated to the matcher's scale (tag 0.4, capability 0.3, trigger 0.8, name 0.9) — a higher threshold makes tag-only and capability-only matches unreachable. |

## `[swarm]`

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_agents` | integer | `5` | The decompose step targets this; the runner clamps to 2–8. |
| `merge_results` | bool | `true` | `false` (or a failed synthesis) concatenates per-agent results under their labels. |
| `agent_timeout_secs` | integer | `300` | Per-agent wall clock; a stuck agent is cancelled and retried. `0` disables. |
| `agent_retries` | integer | `1` | Extra attempts after a timeout or provider error. |

## `[tools]`

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auto_check` | bool | `false` | After a successful write, run the project check (Cargo, tsc, ruff, go vet) and append diagnostics to the next prompt. |
| `auto_lsp` | bool | `true` | After a successful write, run language-server diagnostics on the touched files and append them to the next prompt. Cheap; no-op without a server on `PATH`. |

Write approval behaviour comes from the [policy presets](/guides/policy/), not from a config flag.

## `[lsp]`

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auto_diagnostics` | bool | `true` | Run language-server diagnostics after a write and append them to the next prompt. Cheap; a no-op when no server is on `PATH`. |
| `settle_ms` | u64 | `500` | How long to wait for the server to settle before reading diagnostics. |
| `deferred_enabled` | bool | `true` | Queue diagnostics that arrive late and attach them to the next turn instead of dropping them. |
| `deferred_settle_ms` | u64 | `12000` | How long a deferred pass waits before giving up on a slow server. |

`[tools] auto_lsp` is the coarse switch; `[lsp]` tunes the behaviour once it is on.

## `[security.redact]`

Controls the prompt-path redactor. Log-write redaction is always on and not configurable.

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `in_prompt` | bool | `false` | Run the redactor over every message and tool result before it reaches the model. Default off: a normal code-editing session needs un-redacted file contents. |
| `redact_argument_paths` | array of globs | `[]` | Blank the `arguments` of any tool call whose path matches, independent of `in_prompt`. Stronger than result redaction — the model never sees the arguments at all. |

Both settings replace a secret with `[REDACTED:<rule>]`, which the model cannot round-trip.

`kod` also installs a secret-placeholder vault at startup, by default: it loads (or creates) `~/.kod/secret-placeholder.key` and registers every secret-shaped environment variable, then the wire layer swaps a registered secret for a reversible placeholder the model can reason about. That is a separate mechanism from the redactor above and runs whether or not `in_prompt` is set. A failure to create the key file is logged and leaves placeholders disabled for the session — the pre-vault behaviour — rather than aborting startup.

## `[limits]`

Session and per-turn caps. `0` disables any individual limit.

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_cost_usd_per_session` | f64 | `0` | Total spend ceiling for the session, in USD. |
| `max_cost_usd_per_turn` | f64 | `0` | Per-turn spend ceiling. |
| `max_input_tokens_per_turn` | integer | `0` | Cap on the prompt side of one turn. |
| `max_output_tokens_per_turn` | integer | `0` | Cap on the completion side of one turn. |
| `on_exhausted` | `ask` \| `stop` \| `continue` | `ask` | What to do when a cap is hit. `ask` pauses for a prompt (TUI only; a non-interactive caller treats it as `stop`), `stop` ends the turn keeping the partial reply, `continue` logs a warning and keeps going. |
| `soft_warn_at` | f64 | `0.5` | Warn when spend crosses this fraction of a cap. |
| `tools` | table | `{}` | Per-tool quotas, keyed by tool name; `"default"` applies to any tool not otherwise listed. |

A per-tool quota has `per_turn`, `per_session`, and — for `execute_command` — `per_command`, which limits how many times the same command string may run in one turn.

## `[jev]`

The [TypeSafe AI](https://typesafe.ai) integration. Opt-in; off by default.

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | bool | `false` | Master switch. When false every call site falls back to the pre-Jev heuristic without a network call. |
| `api_key` | string | unset | Explicit key. Falls back to `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`. Never written in the clear — `kod config show-merged` and `kod config export` emit `[redacted]`. |
| `base_url` | string | unset | API root. Falls back to `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL`, then the public endpoint. Set this for a self-hosted gateway. |

## `[hooks]`

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | bool | `false` | Master switch for both hook maps. |
| `pre_tool_use` | map: tool → command template | — | Runs before matching tool calls; `{path}`-style placeholders substituted from call arguments. |
| `post_tool_use` | map: tool → command template | — | Runs after matching tool calls. |

<Code lang="toml" code={`[hooks]
enabled = true
pre_tool_use  = { write_file = "rustfmt {path}" }
post_tool_use = { write_file = "cargo check" }`} />

## `[mcp.servers.<name>]`

One block per MCP server; absent `[mcp]` means no plugins. A failing server is logged and skipped — one broken plugin never blocks the built-ins.

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | string | — | Program to spawn, resolved against `$PATH`. Empty commands are skipped. |
| `args` | string[] | `[]` | Arguments to the program. |
| `env` | map: string → string | — | Added to the child's environment (parent env is inherited). |
| `enabled` | bool | `true` | `false` keeps the block as a record without spawning. |
| `call_timeout_secs` | integer | `60` | Per-call timeout for `tools/call`. |

Tools are exposed to the model as `mcp:<server>.<tool>`.

## `[commands]`

User-defined TUI slash commands. Each key registers `/key`; `{args}` in the value is replaced by everything typed after the command name, `{cwd}` by the working directory.

<Code lang="toml" code={`[commands]
review  = "Review the last change in {cwd} and point out risks."
explain = "Explain what this code does:\\n\\n{args}"`} />

## Project policy: `.kod/policy.toml`

Committed to the repository, layered over the global config (see [Policy & Permissions](/guides/policy/)):

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | `"read-only"` \| `"standard"` \| `"yolo"` | `"standard"` | Coarse baseline for the project. |
| `tools.<name>.mode` | `"allow"` \| `"deny"` \| `"ask"` | — | Overrides the preset for one tool. |
| `tools.<name>.paths` | string[] | — | Allow-list of path globs; unmatched paths are denied. |
| `tools.<name>.forbidden` | string[] | — | Deny globs; deny always wins over allow. |
| `tools.<name>.binaries` | string[] | — | Command allow-list (first token) for `execute_command`. |
| `tools.<name>.forbidden_binaries` | string[] | — | Command deny-list; wins over `binaries`. |
| `tools.<name>.network` | bool | — | Per-tool override of `llm.network_access`. |
| `tools.<name>.domains` | string[] | — | Domain allow-list for `web_fetch`. |
| `git.history_protected` | bool | `true` | Mounts `.git` read-only at the sandbox. |

## Environment variables

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `KOD_SESSION_LOG` | Explicit session log path; default is `~/.kod/sessions/<unix-ms>.jsonl`. |
| `KOD_TUI_STATE_DIR` | Directory for the TUI session and prompt-history files. |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Used by the `cloud-openai` profile (via the endpoint's `api_key_env`). |
| `KOD_TEST_MODEL`, `KOD_TEST_DB` | Live-model test opt-in for contributors; see [Testing](/developers/testing/). |

## Theme: `theme.toml`

A `theme.toml` next to the config selects the TUI palette:

<Code lang="toml" code={`theme = "light"        # or "dark", or a full [theme] table below`} />

A bare `theme = "light"` line is accepted, as is a full `[theme]` table overriding individual ratatui colors (`black`, `red`, `green`, …). Loading is best-effort: an invalid theme file falls back to the default dark theme with a warning rather than failing the session. `kod theme show <name>` prints a built-in palette as JSON.

## Keybindings: `tui_keys.toml` / `.kod-keys.toml`

See [TUI Keybindings](/reference/tui-keys/#rebinding-keys).

<Aside type="tip">
  <code>kod config export -</code> prints the effective config (defaults merged with your edits) to stdout — the fastest way to see every resolved value, including clamped ones.
</Aside>


---

---
title: Crates
description: The 26 crates that make up the KOD workspace, grouped by layer.
sidebar:
  order: 8
type: reference
---

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The KOD workspace is a Cargo workspace with **26 crates** in **4 layers**,
from the most stable foundation to the outermost interface:

- **Foundation** — types, errors, config. No internal dependencies.
- **Engine** — the orchestration core and its five sub-crates under
  `kod-core-*`. See [Core crates](/concepts/core-crates/) for how the
  family fits together.
- **Capability** — providers, tools, skills, memory, transport, and the
  analysis crates (`kod-ast`, `kod-risk`, `kod-minimize`,
  `kod-schema-dialect`). Each is independently usable.
- **Interface** — the `kod` binary (`kod-cli`) and the terminal UI
  (`kod-tui`).

## Foundation

| Crate | Description |
|---|---|
| `kod-types` | IDs, message and tool types, roles, serialization, trust levels, redaction primitives. |
| `kod-error` | `KodError` — the single error enum threaded through every fallible API. |
| `kod-config` | `KodConfig` with its per-section types and mtime-validated TOML cache. |

## Engine

| Crate | Description |
|---|---|
| `kod-core` | The engine: agent loop, transcript, compaction dispatch, telemetry wiring, Jev advisor, swarm runner. |
| `kod-core-routing` | Task classification, context assembly, and model selection. |
| `kod-core-state` | Session persistence, file checkpoints, cost accounting, sensitivity classification. |
| `kod-core-serve` | ACP JSON-RPC server over a Unix-socket daemon, bridging the engine and editor clients. |
| `kod-core-quality` | `snapcompact`, `shake`, and `repomap` — analysis, compaction, and quality gates. |
| `kod-core-tools` | Adapter layer wrapping each `Tool` impl for the engine's dispatch loop. |

## Capability

| Crate | Description |
|---|---|
| `kod-provider` | Provider trait, streaming primitives, retry policy, `TokenUsage`, `testkit` mock providers. |
| `kod-provider-anthropic` | Anthropic Messages API — SSE streaming, cache-control headers, beta gating. |
| `kod-provider-openai` | OpenAI Chat Completions — SSE streaming, tool calling, structured outputs. |
| `kod-ast` | Tree-sitter parsing for 8 languages, with a process-global parse cache. Powers the repo map. |
| `kod-risk` | Command blast-radius classification: parse shell lines, assign `RiskLevel`, flag destructive ops. |
| `kod-schema-dialect` | Per-provider JSON Schema translation and sanitization (dropping unsupported keywords). |
| `kod-minimize` | Shell-output minimizer: head/tail truncation, structured summarisation, `git diff` reduction. |
| `kod-tools` | Tool implementations: `read_file`, `write_file`, `patch_file`, `bash`, `grep`, `web_fetch`, `internal_url` handlers. |
| `kod-skills` | `SKILL.md` parser, matcher (trigram + description-token scoring), and watcher. |
| `kod-memory` | Multi-layer short-term and long-term memory store (redb) with embedding-backed retrieval. |
| `kod-lsp` | Minimal Language Server Protocol client: spawn, diagnostics, code actions. |
| `kod-mcp` | Minimal Model Context Protocol client over stdio: server registration, tool discovery. |
| `kod-swarm` | Multi-agent collaboration: agent communication hub, blackboard, worktree management, yield queue. |
| `kod-telemetry` | OTLP GenAI tracing, span helpers, context injection. |
| `kod-stats` | Session statistics: cost, latency, cache hit rate, per-tool usage. |

## Interface

| Crate | Description |
|---|---|
| `kod-cli` | The `kod` binary: argument parsing, subcommands (`serve`, `checkpoint`, `models`, `init`, `completions`, `update`, …), `fixtures` harness. |
| `kod-tui` | Terminal UI: `KodApp` state, `TuiLoop` event loop, chat widget, syntax highlighting, keybinding table. |

<Aside type="note">
  The **Engine** crates live under `crates/kod-core-*` and form a layered
  subsystem. `kod-core` depends on all five; the sub-crates do not depend
  on `kod-core`. That keeps incremental compilation fast and makes each
  subsystem independently testable.
</Aside>


---

---
title: Skill File Format
description: The exact anatomy of a KOD skill — front matter fields, the three body sections, directory precedence, and validation rules.
sidebar:
  order: 5
type: reference
---

import { Aside, Code, FileTree } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

A skill is a Markdown file with YAML front matter. KOD parses the front matter, splits the body into three sections, caches the result, and matches skills against prompts — with a file watcher enabling hot reload on edit. This page is the exact contract.

## Anatomy

<Code lang="markdown" code={`---
name: rust-refactoring
description: Rust refactoring with idiomatic patterns
version: 1.0.0
category: coding
tags: [rust, refactoring, idioms]
capabilities: [code-refactoring, ownership-analysis]
triggers:
  - "refactor rust"
  - "make more idiomatic"
---

## Instructions

You are an expert Rust refactoring assistant...

## Examples

<example input="Refactor this loop">
...
</example>

## Constraints

- Never change public API without explicit request
- Preserve existing tests`} />

## Front matter fields

| Field | Required | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | Kebab-case identifier; used as the file stem by `kod skills new` and rewritten by `rename`/`copy` so it never drifts from the filename. |
| `description` | yes | One-line summary; searched by `kod skills search` and shown by `kod skills`. |
| `version` | no | Free-form version for the skill itself. (`validate-skills-strict` requires it.) |
| `category` | no | Coarse grouping (`coding`, `testing`, …). |
| `tags` | list | Matching signals — coarser than triggers, finer than category. |
| `capabilities` | list | What the skill enables; also a matching signal. |
| `triggers` | list | Phrases that should activate the skill; matched against the user's prompt. |

## The three body sections

The parser splits the body into:

1. **Instructions** — the operating guidance injected into the model's prompt when the skill matches. This is the skill's main payload.
2. **Examples** — concrete demonstrations. They cost tokens but sharpen behaviour noticeably; keep them small and realistic.
3. **Constraints** — hard rules the model is asked to respect. Put non-negotiables here ("preserve existing tests", "never change the public API").

All three sections reach the model when the skill is matched — none are decorative.

## Directory precedence

KOD discovers skills in four standard directories, in order. Later directories **shadow** earlier ones for skills sharing a name:

1. `~/.kod/skills` — canonical KOD location
2. `~/.agents/skills` — Claude-style compatibility
3. `<project>/.kod/skills` — project-local KOD
4. `<project>/.agents/skills` — project-local Claude-style

Setting `skills.skills_dir` in the config replaces all four with a single custom directory. `kod skills --json` shows the merged inventory exactly as the engine sees it.

## Matching

The matcher scores skills against the prompt using triggers, tags, capabilities, and the name. A skill rides along when its score clears `skills.match_threshold` (default `0.7`), and at most `skills.max_skills_per_query` (default 3) are selected per prompt by the [Task Router](/concepts/router/). Because hot reload is on by default, the next prompt after an edit sees the new content — no restart, no rebuild.

<Aside type="tip">
  A skill that never fires is usually a vocabulary mismatch: the matcher scores word overlap, so triggers should use the words you actually type. <code>kod skills search "&lt;your words&gt;"</code> shows what the matcher sees.
</Aside>

## Validation and CI

Two tools keep a skills directory honest:

- `kod validate-skills` — validates every skill file; exits non-zero on malformed front matter or structure. Wire it into CI so a broken skill fails the pipeline instead of silently never matching.
- `kod validate-skills-strict` — the same, plus a missing `version` field is also a failure.
- `kod skills show <name>` — prints the full file as parsed; if what you wrote is not what you see, the parser is telling you where you diverged.

<FileTree>
- ~/.kod/skills/
  - rust-refactoring.md
  - python-testing.md
  - code-review.md
- my-project/.kod/skills/
  - house-style.md
</FileTree>


---

---
title: Tools Reference
description: The 31 built-in tools — arguments, results, and the safety machinery around each one.
sidebar:
  order: 3
type: reference
---

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

KOD ships 31 built-in tools. Every call goes through the [policy engine](/guides/policy/) before it runs, is executed under a timeout, passes through a per-path advisory lock table, and is recorded (arguments, result, and the policy decision) in the session log. `kod tools list` prints the registry as the model sees it; `kod tools show <name>` prints one tool's full schema.

## File system tools

### `read_file`

Reads a file relative to the engine's working directory. The workhorse for code inspection; allowed under every preset including `read-only`.

### `list_files`

Lists directory contents. Used for orientation before reads — and the same data `kod map` summarises.

### `grep`

Searches file contents. Prefer it when the agent needs to find call sites, definitions, or patterns across many files.

### `search_files`

Finds files by name pattern — the right shape when the agent knows roughly what a file is called but not where it lives.

### `file_info`

Returns metadata (size, type) for a path. Cheap and read-only.

### `write_file`

Creates or overwrites a file. The result attaches a **unified diff** of what changed, and the target file is **snapshot to a checkpoint** before the call executes, so `kod checkpoint restore` can undo it. Gated: `ask` under `standard`, denied under `read-only`.

### `patch_file`

Applies an edit patch to an existing file — the surgical alternative to full rewrites. Shares `write_file`'s safety machinery: unified diff on the result, checkpoint before the call, `ask` under `standard`, denied under `read-only`.

### `edit`

Applies line-addressed edits to a file that was read earlier in the session. The input is a hashline block: a `[path#tag]` header whose tag comes from the `read_file` output, followed by `PUT N.=M:` / `CUT N.=M` / `PUT >$:` operations with `+`-prefixed payload rows. A tag that no longer matches the file refuses the edit rather than applying it to stale content, so an edit cannot silently land on a file that changed underneath it. Shares `write_file`'s safety machinery: unified diff, checkpoint before the call, `ask` under `standard`, denied under `read-only`.

### `jfind`

Semantic code search: describe what you are looking for in plain language and get back files and line ranges rather than exact-string matches. The right tool when `grep` cannot express the query ("where is retry backoff computed"). Without a judge endpoint it degrades to lexical ranking.

### `tool_search`

Finds the tools that can do a task. Given a natural-language description, returns the full schemas of the most relevant tools. Most useful when MCP servers are connected and their tools are not in the visible set.

## Git tools

### `git_status` / `git_diff`

Read-only working-tree status and diff view. Combined, this is how the agent reviews recent changes before suggesting or making edits.

### `git_commit` / `git_branch`

Write-gated git operations: commit the current changes, create a branch. They pass through the same policy engine as file writes — `ask` under `standard`, denied under `read-only` — and inside a sandboxed command context `.git` stays read-only (`git.history_protected`).

## Shell tool

### `execute_command`

Runs a shell command. The most powerful and most gated tool:

- **Policy**: denied outright under `read-only`; `ask` under `standard`; `.kod/policy.toml` can allowlist `binaries` (by first token) and forbid `forbidden_binaries`.
- **Sandbox**: with `--sandbox`, commands run through `bwrap` (Linux) or `sandbox-exec` (macOS), failing loudly when unavailable; `.git` is mounted read-only by default (`git.history_protected`).
- **Hooks**: `pre_tool_use` / `post_tool_use` templates can wrap every execution.

<Aside type="caution">
  Command allowlists are ergonomics, not containment — <code>binaries = ["bash"]</code> allows everything bash can do. Real containment comes from the sandbox primitive.
</Aside>

## Batch tool

### `batch`

Runs several tool calls in one step. Each invocation names a tool and its parameters; results come back in the same order. Use it to read several files, or run several independent searches, without paying a round trip per call.

## Project check tool

### `check`

Runs the compiler or linter that matches the project — Cargo, `tsc`, `ruff`, or `go vet` — and returns structured diagnostics. Read-only by nature. The agent calls it after edits to ask "did that break the build?"; the TUI's `/check` runs it on demand, and `tools.auto_check = true` runs it automatically after every write (off by default — it is a compiler invocation per write).

## Planning and interaction tools

### `todo`

Maintains a visible task list for multi-step work, so progress survives context pressure and you can see the plan alongside the transcript.

### `plan_update`

Updates the session's plan: mark the current step done, add a note, insert a step, or remove one. Keeping the plan in sync with what is actually happening is what makes progress visible to the user.

### `ask_user`

Lets the agent stop and ask you a question instead of guessing — one more reason unattended runs should use `read-only` (there is nobody to answer there either).

## Memory tools

### `memory_save` / `memory_search`

Direct access to the long-term store: persist a durable fact, search existing entries. Registered only when memory is enabled; see [Memory](/guides/memory/) for storage locations and the `kod memory` management commands.

## Swarm tools

### `swarm_note` / `swarm_read` / `hub` / `advise`

A shared blackboard for concurrent agents: one agent publishes findings (`note`), others read them (`read`). Always registered; outside a swarm they are simply an empty blackboard.

`hub` is the coordinator's interface — `list`, `send`, `inbox`, `jobs` — for directing a running swarm rather than exchanging notes. `advise` raises an observation for the primary agent; noise (`stop`, `lgtm`) and duplicates are dropped, so an advisor can be chatty without flooding the transcript.

## LSP tools

### `lsp_diagnostics` / `lsp_definition` / `lsp_references` / `lsp_hover`

Language-server-backed answers: current diagnostics for a file, where a symbol is defined, where it is referenced, and hover documentation. Each tool finds the right server for the file's language on your `PATH` (rust-analyzer, typescript-language-server, …) and **errors naming the missing binary** when there is none — never a silent empty result. The same diagnostics are appended automatically after writes when `tools.auto_lsp` is true (the default).

## Web tool

### `web_fetch`

Fetches an HTTP/HTTPS URL and returns its content. Guards:

- **SSRF protection**: loopback, private, link-local, and metadata endpoints are refused outright.
- **Network opt-in**: disabled unless `llm.network_access` is true — or the tool's own policy entry sets `network = true`.
- **Domain allow-list**: `.kod/policy.toml` can restrict `web_fetch` to named `domains` (e.g. `["docs.rs", "crates.io"]`).

## MCP tools

Tools contributed by configured [MCP servers](/guides/configuration/) are registered under the naming policy `mcp:<server>.<tool>` — for example `mcp:filesystem.read_file` — and appear in `kod tools list` alongside the built-ins. Policy entries address them by that full name.

## Decision precedence, in one table

| Layer | Source | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Preset | `read-only` / `standard` / `yolo` | `standard` (default) |
| 2. Global config | `[tools]` / `[llm]` in `config.toml` | `network_access = false` |
| 3. Project policy | `.kod/policy.toml` | `[tools.write_file] mode = "ask"` |
| 4. CLI override | `--preset` flag | `--preset yolo` |

Within a layer, per-tool entries refine the preset; at glob-conflict time **deny always wins over allow**. `kod policy explain <tool> <args>` prints the verdict for a specific call without running it.

<Aside type="note">
  Timeout, path locking, checkpointing, and policy evaluation apply to *every* tool — there is no ungated path to your files. The [Tools guide](/guides/tools/) explains the families and the write follow-ups (LSP, check) in task-oriented terms.
</Aside>


---

---
title: TUI Keybindings
description: Every TUI keybinding (normal and insert mode), how to rebind keys, and every slash command, with what each one does.
sidebar:
  order: 2
type: reference
---

import { Aside, Code } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The TUI is modal: **normal mode** navigates and commands, **insert mode** edits prompts. Press `i` to enter insert mode; `Esc` returns to normal mode (and cancels a running generation). `?` or `h` opens the in-app help overlay at any time.

## Normal mode

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `i` (or `I`) | enter insert mode |
| `Esc` / `Ctrl-C` | cancel the running prompt |
| `j` / `k` | scroll down / up (arrow keys and mouse wheel also work) |
| `g` / `G`, `Home` / `End` | jump to oldest / newest |
| `PgUp` / `PgDn` | scroll by page |
| `t` | toggle tool-output visibility |
| `o` | expand the newest collapsed tool row |
| `Enter` | expand the tool row under focus (chat focus) |
| `f` | start a type-ahead search |
| `n` / `N` | next / previous search match (after `/search`) |
| `y` | copy the last assistant reply |
| `a` (or `Tab`) | open the agent panel |
| `e` | edit your last message |
| `u` | undo a `/clear` |
| `?` (or `h`) | help overlay |
| `q` | quit — asks for confirmation when a generation is running |

## Insert mode

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` | send the prompt |
| `Ctrl+J` (or `Shift+Enter`) | insert a newline |
| `Tab` | cycle completions (slash commands, model names, file paths) |
| `Up` / `Down` | walk prompt history (your unsent draft is kept) |
| `Ctrl+W` | delete the word before the cursor |
| `Ctrl+U` | clear the line before the cursor |
| `Ctrl+K` | kill to the end of the line |
| `Ctrl+Left` / `Ctrl+Right` | jump by word |

## Rebinding keys

Normal-mode single-character keys are configurable. Put a `[keys]` table in `.kod-keys.toml` (project) or `tui_keys.toml` next to your config (global) — each entry maps an **action name** to a key:

<Code lang="toml" code={`[keys]
quit = "Q"
scroll_down = "J"`} />

Recognised action names: `insert`, `quit`, `help`, `panel`, `scroll_up`, `scroll_down`, `top`, `bottom`, `edit_last`, `undo`, `toggle_tools`, `search_prefix`, `copy_last`. Unknown names are ignored, and a corrupt file silently keeps the defaults — key config must never break startup.

## Slash commands

Type `/` in insert mode; the completion popup lists the available commands (Tab to cycle). Custom commands from your config's `[commands]` block appear here too.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/help` | show the help overlay |
| `/clear` | clear the conversation (reversible with `/undo` or `u`) |
| `/clearall` | clear chat + long-term memory + checkpoints (asks for confirmation) |
| `/undo` | undo a `/clear` |
| `/compact` | summarise the conversation to reclaim context headroom |
| `/summarize` | LLM-summarise the session so far |
| `/model [<name>]` | show or switch the model — instantaneous, even mid-generation |
| `/goal <text>` | set a standing goal the agent works toward (`/goal clear` removes it) |
| `/steer <instruction>` | steer a running generation (typing a plain prompt does the same) |
| `/cancel` | cancel the running generation |
| `/retry` | reconnect + resend the last prompt |
| `/edit` | edit your last message |
| `/regenerate` | regenerate the last assistant reply |
| `/delete` | remove the last user + assistant exchange |
| `/system <text>` | override the system prompt (`/system clear` resets) |
| `/skills` | list loaded skills |
| `/tools` | toggle tool output details |
| `/map` | print the repository map (top-level symbols per file) |
| `/check` | run the project compiler/linter (Cargo, tsc, ruff, go vet) |
| `/git-status` | git status --porcelain=v2 in the current directory |
| `/attach <path>` | attach a file to the next prompt |
| `/diff` | show the most recent file diff (from checkpoints) |
| `/checkpoints` | list file checkpoints for this project |
| `/rollback [id]` | restore a file from a checkpoint |
| `/export [path]` | export the session as Markdown |
| `/save <path>` | save the session to a file |
| `/load <path>` | load a session from a JSON file |
| `/branch [label]` | drop a branch-point marker in the transcript |
| `/fork [label]` | save the current chat as a restorable fork |
| `/handoff` | write a handoff document and start a fresh session with it as context |
| `/memory` | long-term memory: `/memory [search <q> \| delete <id> \| clear]` |
| `/context` | visualise context-window usage and session totals |
| `/stats` | per-session statistics: roles, tools, tokens, elapsed |
| `/whoami` | session summary: model, skills, context, paths |
| `/debug` | diagnostics: `/debug last-prompt` dumps the last grounded prompt |
| `/last-prompt` | shortcut for `/debug last-prompt` |
| `/log [N]` | show recent session log entries |
| `/search [<text>]` | search the transcript (`n`/`N` jump between matches) |
| `/grep <regex>` | regex search the chat history |
| `/copy` | copy the last assistant reply |
| `/raw` | print the last assistant reply raw (no decoration) |
| `/theme [dark\|light]` | switch the theme |
| `/pin <n>` / `/unpin <n>` | pin a message so it survives compaction / remove a pin |
| `/reset` | reset transient state: input, search, expansions, attachments |
| `/doctor` | print a diagnostics report (same as `kod doctor`) |
| `/init` | onboarding info: config path, model profiles, next steps |
| `/swarm <goal>` | launch a multi-agent swarm run |
| `/quit` | exit the TUI |
| `/budget` | session cost and limits: `/budget`, `/budget raise <usd>`, `/budget reset` |
| `/limits` | per-tool quotas: `/limits`, `/limits reset` |
| `/policy` | tool policy: `/policy`, `/policy forget <n>` |
| `/plan` | show plan: `/plan next`, `/plan skip`, `/plan note <text>`, `/plan clear` |
| `/plan-mode` | toggle plan mode: `/plan-mode on` / `off` |
| `/decisions` | durable decisions this session: `/decisions drop <id>`, `/decisions clear` |
| `/learned` | list or clear session-scoped learned approvals: `/learned clear` |
| `/trust` | show or clear the round's taint: `/trust show` / `clear` |
| `/review` | spawn a cross-model review of the last assistant turn |
| `/refine <instruction>` | refine the last assistant reply |
| `/prewalk <endpoint/model>` | arm a one-way model handoff |
| `/remember <text>` | store a durable fact in long-term memory |
| `/blackboard` | swarm blackboard: `/blackboard show` / `clear` |
| `/jobs` | list background jobs |
| `/trace` | structured turn traces: `/trace last` / `list` |
| `/jev` | TypeSafe AI integration: `/jev status`, `stats`, `cache clear`, `test` |
| `/wt` | move this session into a worktree carrying uncommitted changes: `/wt [--clean]` |
| `/export-html [path]` | export the session as a self-contained HTML file |

<Aside type="tip">
  The fastest redirect for a run heading the wrong direction is typing a plain prompt while it generates — identical to <code>/steer</code>, and it preserves all work already done.
</Aside>
